{{Quote|For you, Mon, okay. Take that XP-38A there. It's as hot as I have. But, watch it! Steering's real loose.|Barada|<ref name="OFE">{{StoryCite|story=Old Friends: Ephant Mon's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>}}
'''Barada''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] and [[Technician/Legends|mechanic]] who worked as the head of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] pool of [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsor]] vehicles, as well as guard and [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of his own vehicles on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. While Barada should have been able to buy his own freedom with the salary Jabba paid him, the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] had tricked his slave, charging him for room and food and precluding him from being free again. Despite this, Barada was believed to be a loyal servant, with Jabba giving him responsibilities, subordinates, [[Droid/Legends|droids]], and a number of would-be luxuries. Barada was reasonably content with his lot in life, and became friends with Jabba's [[Spy/Legends|spy]] [[Ephant Mon/Legends|Ephant Mon]], although other people at [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]], including the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] drunkard [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]], preyed on Barada.

Not long before the [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]], Barada conspired with Jabba's [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] accountant [[Tessek/Legends|Tessek]] and the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]] to place a bomb on Jabba's [[Ubrikkian Industries/Legends|Ubrikkian]] [[Luxury-class sail barge|luxury sail barge]], with the intent of [[Death/Legends|killing]] the Hutt [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]]. His plot was discovered in advance, but Barada was not informed of this. Soon afterward, Barada drove a [[Skiff/Legends|skiff]] of prisoners to their scheduled execution at the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]]. One of the convicted individuals, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], struggled with Barada and the other guards, and Barada was killed in the ensuing fight.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Where are you going?''"<br />"''Back to work, what else? We're heading for the pit in less than an hour. I just hope you'll be a passenger, not a prisoner.|Ephant Mon and Barada|<ref name="OFE" />}}
Barada was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Klatooinian/Legends|Klatooinian]]<ref name="EGC" /> born on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]],<ref name="GGQ" /> in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Many Klatooinians were [[Barada (name)|named Barada]] after the legendary and revered Klatooinian scholar and leader [[Barada M'Beg]].<ref name="GG12">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] reported that this name was the third most popular baby name of [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref>{{HoloNetNewsWeb|49||A Closer Look}}</ref>  

As a young boy, Barada lived on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Klatooine/Legends|Klatooine]] where he enjoyed feeling the local fresh wind on his face. During this time, he planned to leave his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and travel to a different planet in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] where he intended to live and have various adventures.<ref name="GGQ" /> However, during his youth, Barada behaved disrespectfully to his parents,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="EGC" /> which went against Klatooinian custom<ref name="EGC" /> and was a crime punishable with the sale of the disrespectful son as an indentured servant.<ref name="G2E">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> As such, following tradition, Barada was sold by his parents<ref name="GG" /> to a [[Unidentified garage owner|garage owner]].<ref name="EGC" />

Barada served his new master for a time.<ref name="GG" /> The master in turn followed the letter of the contract and paid Barada a periodic amount as a salary. To earn his freedom, Barada was to pay his master the exact amount he had paid for Barada. Saving his salary, Barada was 2,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] from his freedom,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="EGC" /> and he was to obtain that amount in one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] or less.<ref name="GG" /> At that point, the owner could contract Barada as a free being if he wished so.<ref name="FQP">{{StoryCite|story=A Free Quarren in the Palace: Tessek's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref>

[[File:BaradaECG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Barada]]

The garage owner played a rigged game of [[Sabacc/Legends|sabacc]] with a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] named [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. Jabba gained the garage,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="EGC" /><ref name="DBB">{{DB|character|barada|Barada}}</ref> and also Barada's servitude contract<ref name="G2E" /><ref name="CRD1">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Barada}}</ref> No one dared to accuse Jabba of cheating,<ref name="EGC" /> and thus, Barada found himself indentured to Jabba.<ref name="GG" /> Jabba employed Barada as one of the guards in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|his palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]<ref name="G2E" /> and in several criminal activities. Jabba also ordered Barada to work in the Hutt's fleet of land vehicles,<ref name="DBB" /> or repulsorpool,<ref name="G2E" /> mostly including customized, armored [[Skiff/Legends|skiffs]] for the arid local climate,<ref name="GG" /> vehicles used by Jabba and his workers including the big [[Ubrikkian Industries/Legends|Ubrikkian]] [[Luxury-class sail barge|luxury sail barge]], and the [[Hoversled/Legends|repulsor sleds]] that Jabba used to move his massive person.<ref name="EGC" />

Motivated, Barada advanced and became the head<ref name="PTD">{{StoryCite|story=Payback: The Tale of Dengar|book=Tales of the Bounty Hunters}}</ref> and captain<ref name="DBB" /> of the pool.<ref name="FQP" /> As the local mechanic,<ref name="GGQ" /> his responsibilities included obtaining, customizing, crewing, taking care of,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="G2E" /><ref name="DBB" /> maintaining, and supplying the vehicles.<ref name="CRD1" /> Should the skiff captain [[Ak-Buz]] be too inebriated to serve in this capacity&mdash;something not unheard of<ref name="GGQ" />&mdash;then Barada would also serve as skiff captain,<ref name="GG12" /> especially in combat or if Jabba was on board.<ref name="GG" /><ref name="G2E" />

Jabba noticed Barada's high skills<ref name="EGC" /> and gave the Klatooinian a real responsibility&mdash;something uncommon in the Hutt's entourage.<ref name="GG" /> Barada had several people under his command, including his main assistant, [[Klaatu/Legends|Klaatu]] the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]], charged with repairing the skiffs;<ref name="CRD3">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Klaatu}}</ref> [[Mal Hyb]], a capable female [[Human/Legends|Human]] assistant;<ref name="GGQ" /> and the Human accountant [[Gailid]] who enjoyed tending to skiffs with Barada.<ref name="CRD2">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Gailid}}</ref> Many of the [[Weequay/Legends|Weequays]] at the palace worked directly for Barada,<ref name="CRD4">{{CCG|set=Jabba's Palace Limited|cardname=Weequay Skiff Master}}</ref> even if the Klatooinian had trouble giving them orders or even communicating with them. Barada also had several [[Droid/Legends|droids]] under his command, including an [[AE-35]] unit helping him at the sail barge.<ref name="GGQ" /> Commonly, Barada's droids kept the bay under surveillance.<ref name="FQP" />

Barada was allowed to sleep at the motor pool to protect the vehicles, laying on a bed of sand over a corner of the floor full of stones.<ref name="FQP" /> Barada also had his own bunk,<ref name="GGQ" /> and even a sink at his quarters, even if few of Jabba's minions were allowed such commodities.<ref name="FQP" />

Jabba valued too much Barada's services to allow the mechanic to buy his freedom,<ref name="OFE" /> and as such he developed a ruse to keep him indefinitely indentured. Barada earned the amount his contract specified, but Jabba charged him that exact amount for room and board. Barada had no other source of income,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="EGC" /> and as a consequence he remained indentured.<ref name="OFE" /> The Klatooinian showed a surprising honesty and<ref name="OFE" /> high loyalty to Jabba.<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="PTD" /><ref name="OFE" /> As such, Barada became one of the few bond servants that Jabba trusted.<ref name="FQP" /> This trust was not wisely placed, as Barada was not so fond of Jabba.<ref name="FQP" />

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> Barada worked as mechanic of Jabba's [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] bikes and [[Podracer/Legends|podracers]]. Knowing that Jabba's rival [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Valarian/Legends|Valarian's]] podracers cheated in the illegal races, Barada hired an independent [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] to [[Spy/Legends|spy]] the [[Valarian Pod Racers Bunker]], to discover how they did so. He later hired the spacer to [[Assassin/Legends|assassinate]] Valarian's podracer champion [[Doane Watki]]. In exchange for this service, Barada gave the spacer some money and a [[vehicle customization kit]].<ref name="SWG:JPB">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Jabba's Palace : Barada|Tatooine}}</ref> At some point, Barada also befriended [[Ephant Mon/Legends|Ephant Mon]], a [[Chevin/Legends|Chevin]] staying at Jabba's palace for reasons Mon kept to himself.<ref name="OFE" />
<!--Conspiracy-->
In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Barada placed an order for vehicle parts, but it never reached the Palace and, after several weeks, Barada decided he could give it up for lost.<ref name="GGQ" /> Around that point, Barada joined Jabba's [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] accountant [[Tessek/Legends|Tessek]] and the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]] in a conspiracy to kill Jabba.<ref name="PTD" /> Some of the Weequay guards and [[Ree-Yees/Legends|Ree-Yees]], the [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] drunkard, were also accomplices of Tessek's. Tessek feared that Barada or any other of his other partners-in-crime could be treacherous or sloppy; his worries were so intense that the [[B'omarr Order/Legends|B'omarr monks]] in the Palace discovered them by reading Tessek's mind.<ref name="FQP" /> Dengar agreed to build a bomb and giving it to Barada; the trusted Klatooinian would then place the artifact in Jabba's barge.<ref name="PTD" />

Three days later, Dengar finished the bomb and approached Barada. The bounty hunter was unaware of his rival, [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], having placed a [[Transmitter/Legends|microtransmitter]] in one of his holsters. Fett recorded the conversation between Barada and Dengar when the bomb changed hands, and obtained proofs of the assassination attempt involving Barada, Dengar, and Tessek. Barada then hid the bomb at the barge, arranging it to explode two days later.<ref name="PTD" />

The following day, an [[Anzat (species)|Anzati]]<ref name="OOTC">{{StoryCite|story=Out of the Closet: The Assassin's Tale|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref> assassinated barge captain Ak-Buz. The corpse was found by Jabba's chef [[Porcellus/Legends|Porcellus]] who, panicked, hid it in the machine yard when neither Barada or his Weequays were there.<ref name="TCC">{{StoryCite|story=Taster's Choice: The Tale of Jabba's Chef|book=Tales from Jabba's Palace}}</ref> Meanwhile, Fett reported the conspiracy to Jabba. Jabba decided to secretly defuse the bomb and punish Tessek by forcing the Quarren to go with Jabba when the explosion was scheduled. Jabba, who found the situation to be funny, decided to procrastinate Barada's punishment for several weeks; and, admitting that Denger was dangerous, allowed Fett to punish his peer.<ref name="PTD" /> Once Jabba had told Tessek he requested his presence on the barge, Tessek planned to escape on a speeder bike, but he needed one skilled operator to open the palace blast doors, and he could not ask Barada as Jabba would kill the Klatooinian for that, and Barada knew it.<ref name="FQP" />

During that day, [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] sneaked in Jabba's Palace disguised as a [[Ubese/Legends|Ubese]] along with her friend, [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]], in an attempt to free her lover, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], who had been captured by Jabba. Jabba discovered and stopped the plot, and sent Solo and Chewbacca to his dungeons, keeping the Princess chained to him as a slave.<ref name="ROTJ" />
<!--Day of ROTJ-->
Barada began the following day looking for six [[rocker-panel cotter pin]]s for his AE-35 at the scrap heap next to the palace. He was joined in his walk by two Weequay guards who did not speak their intentions. Barada found Ak-Buz's corpse in the heap and the Weequays, suddenly interested, took the body. Barada mentioned that there had been other unsolved murders in the palace; then, the Weequays signed Barada to not delve any more on that because it was the Weequay guards' business. Barada obeyed, and decided that he had been automatically promoted to permanent captain of the sail barge.<ref name="GGQ" />

Barada returned to his garage and buried his head in one engine compartment. Mon came for a pre-scheduled visit and asked Barada for a quick skiff. While Barada was initially reluctant to give away any but the more common vehicles, he accepted to lend his friend a quick [[XP-38A utility landspeeder]], warning him about its steering. Mon used it to travel to the [[Lucky Despot]] hotel and back.<ref name="OFE" />

Jabba and Barada also discovered the identity, and importance, of Jabba's new female slave; the Hutt laughed at the importance of his captive. Barada was then visited by Tessek, who wanted to confirm if the Klatooinian had hidden the bomb in the sail barge. Barada eased him discreetly, but he also explained that Jabba had chained the Princess of Alderaan, a high-ranking member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], and Tessek assumed that the Rebels would probably stage a daring rescue. Barada added that Jabba feared not the Rebels. Tessek left Barada's garage just in time for the arrival of a Rebel agent, [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="FQP" />

Skywalker offered to negotiate with Jabba for Solo's life and, when this failed, threatened Jabba. Jabba confronted Skywalker with his favorite monster, the [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]], but Skywalker killed it. Enraged, Jabba ordered to take Skywalker, Solo and Chewbacca to the [[Great Pit of Carkoon/Legends|Great Pit of Carkoon]], where they were to be thrown into the [[Sarlacc/Legends|sarlacc]], and to be digested slowly for one thousand years.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Barada was notified, as he had only hours to get the sail barge ready.<ref name="FQP" /> Mon came back soon afterward, and Barada told his friend about all the events he had missed.<ref name="OFE" />

Barada and his team<ref name="GGQ" /> spent hours painstakingly reviewing the barge's engine and many other details.<ref name="OFE" /> The Klatooinian did not allow a traditional one-hour meal break until the AE-35 had been repaired and replaced, as he feared punishment should anything failed during the Hutt's pleasure trip.<ref name="GGQ" />

Ephant Mon came again to confide with Barada during this time: After a conversation with the Jedi prisoner, Mon believed that the Jedi could kill Jabba, and wanted to convince the Hutt to pardon the convicted people. Barada answered that Jabba would not believe that and probably would execute Mon too. Mon explained that he could simply leave, but he explained to Barada that Jabba had saved Mon's life on [[Glakka]] and, feeling morally in debt with the Hutt, Mon had protected his friend from conspiracies. Barada was aghast at Mon's secret, but nonetheless told Mon that, in his opinion, the debt had been repaid. The Jedi had also opened Mon's eyes and made him wish to return to a simpler life, but Barada was unable to understand Mon's explanation on this subject. The mechanic returned to work and wished to see Mon again as a free Chevin.<ref name="OFE" />

Soon afterward, five Weequays concluded that Ak-Buz's assassin had hidden a bomb in Jabba's sail barge. They intended to board the vehicle to investigate, but Barada refused to let them in. The Weequays bribed him with food, specifically [[beignet]]s cooked by Porcellus.<ref name="GGQ" />

Barada was not asked to captain the sail barge. Instead, he was to captain a gunskiff which would escort the skiff<ref name="ROTJN">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' novel]]</ref> containing the prisoners through the desert. The Prisoner skiff was manned by several guards including two Weequay guards and a third security agent&mdash;who was secretly [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]], an undercover friend of Solo who was waiting for a chance to release him and throw the guards overboard. Barada took a [[Vibro-ax/Legends|vibro-ax]] and watched the prisoners menacingly, as if daring them to misbehave; the Weequays he traveled with gave the same impression.
[[File:Barada-FF88.png|thumb|right|190px|Barada]]
The skiffs and the barge reached the Great Pit of Carkoon. Barada stopped his skiff to hover over a hole in the sand where the sarlacc waited. A plank was released from the prisoners skiff, and [[Pagetti Rook/Legends|Pagetti Rook]], one of the Weequays, pushed Skywalker to it. Skywalker jumped from the plank, grabbed its edge with a hand while falling, and jumped back to the skiff in an athletic feat.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Barada and the other guards were confused at this,<ref name="ROTJN" /> and Skywalker used his initiative to catch a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] that was timely ejected by the droid [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. Skywalker activated the saber and attacked the guards. Barada and the guards on the second skiff then reacted by shooting at Skywalker, while Calrissian struggled with the helmsbeing.<ref name="ROTJ" />

Skywalker and Calrissian quickly killed all of the guards on the first skiff and the Jedi leapt to the second attacking the guards there.<ref name="ROTJ" /> Barada was slashed by Skywalker in the ensuing fight,<ref name="DBB" /> his body falling into the gaping maw of the sarlacc<ref name="EGC" /> under the watching eyes of Tessek.<ref name="FQP" /> [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon|The battle]] went on, ending in a victory of the Alliance and the deaths of Jabba and, eventually, of many of his followers.<ref name="ROTJ" />
<!--Legacy-->
Barada was survived by his co-conspirators [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]]<ref name="PTD" /> and Tessek. The Quarren escaped the barge and went back to the Palace. Delirious for the lack of water, he assumed that trusted Barada was opening the Palace's blast doors for him, and went to the pool to ask him for water before realizing that Barada had died. Tessek then used Barada's sink to re-moisturize before leaving the pool.<ref name="FQP" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Not a chance. We've got the barge all tuned up and I don't want you leather-faced bullies wrecking it.|Barada to the Weequay guards|<ref name="GGQ" />}}
<!--Physical description-->
Barada was a male Klatooinian with leathery<ref name="EGC" /> green skin<ref name="ROTJ" /> that had been described as brown;<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="FQP" /> Tessek the Quarren found it similar to the deserts of Tatooine both in color and texture.<ref name="FQP" /> The Klatooinian was hairless, having a skull crest<ref name="EGC" /> that sometimes changed to bright red.<ref name="FQP" /> Barada's red eyes<ref name="EGC" /> gleamed dimly with a shade of yellow when the lights were low;<ref name="FQP" /> he had to shade the eyes or skint to withstand very bright lights.<ref name="GGQ" /> His face also included a canine snout<ref name="DBB" /> that allowed him to smell items.<ref name="GGQ" /> and a constant scowl.<ref name="OFE" /> At some point after his youth, his face was heavily scarred.<ref name="GGQ" />

At 1.7 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] of height,<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="DBB" /> Barada was ten centimeters shorter than the average Klatooinian.<ref name="DBK">{{DB|species|klatooinian|Klatooinian}}</ref> His strong hands were nonetheless very big.<ref name="GGQ" />
<!--Personality-->
A good-natured and earnest fellow,<ref name="OFE" /> Barada was also a remorseless<ref name="TOY4">''The Saga Collection'' action figures (2006) [https://www.rebelscum.com/tsc004barada.asp]</ref> and violent minion, lacking any sophistication.<ref name="DBB" /> Barada was also one of Jabba's most hard-working servants,<ref name="EGC" /> having found a reason to live in his work<ref name="DBB" /> and taking it to heart.<ref name="G2E" /> He was demanding and strict<ref name="ROTJN" /> especially with his subordinates, fearing a strong reprisal from Jabba should anything under his responsibility go wrong.<ref name="GGQ" />

While he was mostly a slave, Barada was not completely unhappy with his lot, as he found most of his needs to be covered. He was also free to dream about his youth,<ref name="GGQ" /> something he did while sleeping topless.<ref name="FQP" /> He was unable to obtain money,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="EGC" /> but he was sometimes bribed with food.<ref name="GGQ" />

Barada was quite intelligent and secretive,<ref name="FQP" /> able to deduce that Ak-Buz had been murdered by an Anzat because the corpse had no marks. He could also blaspheme in several languages. However, he was perceived as dim-witted by the Weequays,<ref name="GGQ" /> and also by Ree-Yees, who was considered a fool himself but believed that Barada was even more foolish and thus a mark for his scams.<ref name="GG" /><ref name="DBR">{{DB|character|reeyees|Ree-Yees}}</ref> Tessek was scared of Barada being too stupid to follow his scheme,<ref name="FQP" /> and Ephant Mon found him unable to understand his Force-induced epiphany.<ref name="OFE" />

Barada was good at repairing several kinds of technologies, including [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] vehicles, armor, land vehicles, droids, and hover vehicles. He was also a capable repulsorlift [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]].<ref name="GG" /> Barada was a formidable melee fighter,<ref name="GG" /><ref name="TOY4" /> but he was also good in a shootout using<ref name="GG" /> his weapon of choice, the [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]]. He also carried with him a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]],<ref name="GG" /><ref name="EGC" /><ref name="DBB" /> a [[Vibro-ax/Legends|vibro-ax]]<ref name="DBB" /> and a mechanic tool kit.<ref name="GG" /> His vehicles of choice were the Ubrikkian luxury sail barge<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="DBB" /> and the desert skiff.<ref name="DBB" />
<!--Friends-->
Barada was mostly a loner,<ref name="EGC" /> but he found a friend in the Chevin Ephant Mon.<ref name="OFE" /><ref name="EGC" /> While Mon was unable to take Barada away from his responsabilities as a mechanic, he liked the young Klatooinian. Barada, in turn, was observant enough to read in the facial expressions of his friend.<ref name="OFE" /> Mon trusted Barada and commonly asked for his advice and, as Mon was a traitor-seeking spy, this made Barada one of the best informed people in Jabba's entourage.<ref name="EGC" /> However, Mon did not trust Barada with his secret past until the last time they met.<ref name="OFE" />

Barada disliked the company of the Weequays. He believed they were inscrutable, ruthless fighters, and had never heard them speaking. However, Barada did his best to understand what they wanted, and only if he failed at doing so, he opted to ignore them.<ref name="GGQ" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Gort, Klaatu barada nikto. Klaatu barada nikto.|Helen Benson (played by [[Wikipedia:Patricia Neal|Patricia Neal]]) in the film [[Wikipedia:The Day The Earth Stood Still|''The Day The Earth Stood Still'']]|<ref name="DESS">{{VisualMediaCite|title=[[Wikipedia:The Day The Earth Stood Still|''The Day The Earth Stood Still'']]|director=[[Wikipedia:Robert Wise|Robert Wise]]|prod=[[20th Century Studios]]|year=[[1950s|1951]]}}</ref>}}
Barada first appeared in [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|the novelization of ''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="ROTJN" /> He went on to appear in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|the homonymous movie]],<ref name="ROTJ" /> for which he was developed as one of the skiff guards. Concept sketches on him were drawn, and later maquettes were crafted. Barada was executed as a costume made of a slip-on mask and gloves representing hands. Several "Barada-like" aliens were crafted for the scene of the sarlacc.<ref name="DBK" /> In [[1997]], Barada's mask was re-used for a new character, [[Umpass-stay/Legends|Umpass-stay]], in [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'' (Special Edition)]].<ref name="DBK" />

In the short story "[[The Great God Quay: The Tale of Barada and the Weequays]]," Barada is mistakenly described as being in the place of [[Kithaba/Legends|Kithaba]] on the prisoner skiff and being the first guard to die after being sliced in half by Luke Skywalker. However, in the film he is clearly not aboard the prisoner skiff but on the second, where he is later pushed off into the mouth of the sarlacc. It is possible Barada in fact survived for some time in the stomach of the sarlacc as Boba Fett did.

Barada's name comes from the line "[[Wikipedia:Klaatu barada nikto|''Klaatu barada nikto'']]" which is used in the classic science-fiction film [[Wikipedia:The Day The Earth Stood Still|''The Day The Earth Stood Still'']] ([[1950s|1951]]), along with the [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] skiff guards [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="DBB" /><ref name="DBN">{{DB|species|nikto|Nikto}}</ref> and Klaatu's name. In ''The Day The Earth Stood Still,'' the Human-looking alien Klaatu, played by Michael Rennie, is sent to jail but asks his friend Helen Benson, played by Patricia Neal, to go to his robot companion Gort should anything happen to him and utter the sentence&mdash;whose meaning is never specified&mdash;prompting Gort to revive Klaatu.<ref name="DESS" />The section on Barada at the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] of [[StarWars.com]] mistakenly says the the mute Gort utters the sentence,<ref name="DBB" /> while the section on Nikto says that it is Klaatu who utters it to control the giant robot Gort&mdash;but in the movie, Klaatu never says it to Gort directly.<ref name="DBN" /> The sentence was re-used in several other unrelated movies as a homage, including ''Tron,'' ''Toys'' and ''Army of Darkness.''

[[Kenner Products|Kenner]] and [[Hasbro]] released a Barada action figure several separate times. The first one came out in [[1985]] as part of the original 'Power of the Force' series, with an item called "Skiff guard battle staff", and was one of the 'Last 17' figures issued in the 'vintage' era. The color scheme and weapon used, though, actually come from another Klatooinian guard, Kithaba.<ref name="TOY1">[[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1985 toy line)|''Star Wars: The Power of the Force'' toy line (1985)]] [https://www.rebelscum.com/VINtBarada.asp]</ref> A true rendering of Barada was released 14 years later, as part of the "Jabba's Skiff Guards" cinema scene ([[1999]]), in the revived 'Power of the Force' line, equipped with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]]. The pack included the Nikto called [[Vizam/Legends|Vizam]] and Klaatu&mdash;even if, during ''Return of the Jedi,'' Klaatu is seen in the sail barge, not on the skiff.<ref name="TOY2">[[Star Wars: The Power of the Force (1995 toy line)|''Star Wars: The Power of the Force'' toy line (1995)]] [https://www.rebelscum.com/POTF2jabbasskiffguards.asp]</ref> A similar figure was rereleased in [[2004]] as part of a [[Battle of the Great Pit of Carkoon]]-themed multipack exclusive to Toys "R" Us, with figures of Han Solo, Klaatu, and Nikto. Except for Solo, the package confuses the names: Barada is called Klaatu, and Vizam the Nikto is called Barada.<ref name="TOY3">''Skirmish at Carkoon'' multipack (Toys R Us Exclusive) [https://www.rebelscum.com/sw04skirmishatcarkoon.asp]</ref> In [[2006]], the figure was re-released as "Barada (Skiff Guard)" for the initial wave of ''The Saga Collection'', along with a blaster, a display stand, and a mock [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]].<ref name="TOY4" />

In the [[Dark Horse Comics]] issue [[Tales of the Jedi 4|''Tales of the Jedi'' 4]], a group of individuals is said to include "Baradas,"<ref name="TOTJ">[[Tales of the Jedi 4|''Tales of the Jedi'' 4]]</ref> potentially a misidentification of the Klatooinian species.

Barada's name is mentioned in passing in the book ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'', as one of the example names for Klatooinians,<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> and indirectly when talking about the many Klatooinians named after Barada M'Beg in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="NEGAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>

The [[Star Wars Trading Card Game]] from [[Decipher]] includes a card representing Barada. This character is fairly strong, having a bonus to be ''very'' strong if he is inside Jabba's Palace, but he loses almost all his advantage if he leaves Tatooine. In this game, Barada can also recover lost transport vehicles.<ref name="CRD1" />
